title: Deprecate legacy build scripts and introduce fanout remote-cache + layer trimming
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Background: Our legacy shell-based build orchestration (scripts/build_*.sh + matrix.yml) introduced significant variability in layer ordering, redundant dependency installs, and noisy CI runs. This causes long cold-builds, large Docker layers, and high flakiness in lint/test jobs. Goal: Replace the legacy scripts with a BuildKit-first pipeline that uses a fanout remote cache (per-language TTLs and shard keys), standardize slimmer base images, and remove duplicated install steps. Deliverables: 1) Migration plan and compatibility shim so active branches keep building. 2) New CI jobs that use mounted caches + remote CAS for heavy language toolchains. 3) Dockerfile rewrite guidelines + automated linter to detect expensive layer patterns. 4) Toolchain upgrade plan for Node/Go/Rust lint runners and stabilized lint-only runners. 5) Canary rollout and observability dashboards (cache hit rate, median cold build time, job CPU/GPU allocation). Trade-offs and decisions: - We will keep the legacy scripts for 2 weeks behind a feature flag in CI to enable rollback for release branches. - Absolute layer ordering guarantees are infeasible for some legacy images; we will instead enforce reproducible layering for new and actively maintained services. - Remote CAS improves cache hit rates but requires pre-warm jobs and cache shard keys; we prioritized shard-by-language+major-version to avoid cache poisoning between semver-incompatible installs. Implementation notes: - Build pipeline: switch to buildkit invocation via buildctl with --export-cache=type=registry,ref=registry.redwood-ci/cache:cache-v2 and --import-cache for pull-through. - Create priming workflow (ci/prime-cache) that runs nightly on changed language toolchains. - Introduce a 'slimbase' family derived from ubuntu-minimal with pinned OS packages and a layer that installs only the language runtimes as separate optional stages. - Add a pre-merge check that runs dockerfile-layer-checker (dockerfile-lint + custom script) to reject images with layers > 50MB or > 20 RUN instructions. - Lint/toolchain changes: upgrade eslint to 9.x, typescript to 5.x where compatible, Go toolchains to 1.21 and add go mod vendor step to reduce remote downloads. - CI matrix: split fast-fail lightweight tests (unit+lints) from full-matrix integration builds; only the full-matrix uses remote CAS exports. Rollout plan: 1) Week 0: merge docs + CI flagging; enable on a small set of non-critical services (billing-tools, infra-utils). 2) Week 1-2: run priming, monitor cache hit rates and pipeline latency. 3) Week 3: enable for all active microservices; deprecate legacy scripts and remove after 2-week stabilization. Metrics to track: - Cold build median time (target -40%) - Cache hit ratio per-language (target >70% steady) - CI concurrency / credit consumption (target -30%) - Lint runner failures due to environment changes (target <2%) Backlinks and artifacts: - Confluence RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/CI+Remote+Cache+and+Slim+Base+RFC - Draft Dockerfile guidelines: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1example
  - Tracking dashboard for cache metrics: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-cache/ci-cache-overview
  - Implementation PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1345
  - Priming workflow PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1361

Notes on risks and mitigations: - Risk: Cache poisoning across versions -> Mitigation: include semver shard key and purge strategy via tag TTL. - Risk: Increased CI flakiness after toolchain upgrades -> Mitigation: opt-in upgrade per repo with a canary label and revertable commit. - Risk: Unexpected image size regressions -> Mitigation: pre-merge size check and autobisect script that points to offending Dockerfile lines.
